intent: Tools image: JDK-free container image with the CLI, launcher and exec wrapper, run inside the app image
Tools image, launcher guards, image workflow and Docker end-to-end check

title: ship a JDK-free tools image that runs inside the application image
why: An archive is valid only for the application's own JDK build, JAR content, paths and modification times, so the tool must run where those files are. One busybox-based image works for every JDK via copy-at-deploy or COPY --from.
alternative: Per-JDK images with a bundled JDK (the issue's wording) — rejected: cannot see the application's JARs, fingerprints would not match

title: launcher skips fetch and run with exit 0 when Java is missing or older than 21
why: An init container or entrypoint that fails blocks the pod; an old Java cannot run the CLI, so the safest result is no cache. Other commands fail loudly (2 or 127).
alternative: Let the JVM fail with UnsupportedClassVersionError — rejected: exit 1 would stop the pod

title: check the image with a Docker end-to-end script that is also a CI job
why: Unit tests cannot show that the launcher, the copy pattern, a real registry, fetch and the exec wrapper work together in an application image; the script trains on JDK 21 (AppCDS) and 25 (AOT), asserts the app class comes from the archive, java is PID 1 and a changed -Xmx falls back.
alternative: Test only the Java code — rejected: the packaging is what #16 delivers

name: tools image
role: Carries mnemo-warmup.jar, launcher and exec wrapper into the application image
conditions: No JDK; application image needs Java 21+; distroless apps use run --spawn

name: verify-image.sh
role: Docker end-to-end check on JDK 21 and 25 with a local registry plus launcher guard checks
conditions: Needs Docker and network for image pulls

subject: Tool and app must share files
why: Training and running must see the same JAR path and modification time, so the script mounts one volume at /app in every container

subject: java -version output
why: JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS adds a Picked up line on stderr, so the launcher greps for the version line instead of using line 1

intent: Address review: launcher run fallback, README init example, pinned release revision, scoped cleanup

title: launcher starts the original command for run when Java is unusable
why: Exiting 0 without starting the application terminates the container. For run the launcher now execs the command after -- unchanged (print mode still prints nothing so the wrapper keeps its own fallback).
alternative: Exit 0 for every skipped command — rejected: direct run and --spawn entrypoints would stop the application

title: resolve the release revision once to a SHA and use it in verify and publish
why: On manual dispatch verify checked out the dispatch ref while publish checked out the tag, so a published image could differ from the verified one; a moving tag could also change between jobs.
alternative: Checkout the tag in each job — rejected: not the same commit guaranteed

title: give every verify-image.sh resource a per-run id and remove only what the run created
why: A name-pattern cleanup deleted other volumes on developer machines and in concurrent runs. Names are registered in the parent shell; registering inside a command substitution silently loses the tracking.
alternative: Delete everything matching mw-verify- — rejected: removes other people's resources

subject: Bash arrays and command substitution
why: A function called inside $(...) runs in a subshell, so appending to a parent array there is lost; the leaked volumes showed it

subject: Shell-free application images
why: No launcher can run there, so an old Java makes a direct java -jar init container fail and block the pod; document Java 21+ as a requirement
